text:
sarah: Quick question — before we flip the automatic fallback policy for public APIs, can we add a "simulate" run in the console? Want to validate no noisy cascading failovers to smaller models.

jordan: Yes please. We had a brief outage last month where a bad threshold knocked a bunch of requests into the slow path. A dry-run that replays recent traffic would have caught it.

kevin: Agreed. UX idea: a modal that lets you select a time window + traffic slice (percentile by tenant) and then shows a step-by-step playback of actions taken. Each step shows the trigger matched, evaluated metrics, and the planned action.

maya: Also need to make sure the simulation emits the same audit records as a real run (for compliance). Exportable JSON lines so security can ingest into the SIEM.

anne: UX note — show estimated error impact (e.g., requests rerouted, expected latency delta) and an inline toggle for "apply rollout after review". Keep the modal small so it fits ops screens.

kevin: Implementation sketch (server-side): run the policy engine on captured metrics stream but only write to a staging audit table, not the live routing layer. Example policy payload for testing:

```json
{
  "id": "pf-340",
  "version": "1",
  "triggers": [
    {"type": "latency_p95", "window_s": 60, "threshold_ms": 1200},
    {"type": "http5xx_rate", "window_s": 60, "threshold_pct": 0.5}
  ],
  "action": {"mode": "failover", "target": "small-model-v2"},
  "audit": true
}
```

jordan: Nice. Two questions: 1) During sim, do we model capacity on the target? If target gets saturated in sim we should flag it. 2) Can sim output a confidence score for non-deterministic triggers (e.g., sampling-based quotas)?

kevin: For (1) we can run a simple capacity estimate based on recent throughput and observed p95 token generation. Flag as "potential saturation" if projected qps > 80% of historical capacity. For (2) we surface probabilistic triggers and show the sampled variance.

maya: On audit exports — make sure the record schema includes the source trace id and the exact policy version applied. Example audit line: 

2025-08-24T12:03:22Z | trace=tr_3f9a | policy=pf-340@v1 | action=simulate:switched->small-model-v2 | reason=latency_p95(1245ms)

deploy-bot: [auto-test] ran sim-policy pf-340 against 15m of prod-ish traffic: 1.2% of requests would have failed over, 0.04% potential saturation on small-model-v2. Logs: https://internal-ci/runs/6789

sarah: Perfect — can we add a checkbox to include "canary fallback" vs "global fallback" in the sim? We want to validate rollout behaviors (gradual ramp) too.

anne: UX: in the playback timeline allow zoom to route-level granularity so PMs can inspect a single tenant's behavior. Also add an inline link "view audit JSON" for each step.

kevin: One more thing: simulate the downstream metrics the fallback will produce (embedding counts, token cost delta) so billing team can sign off. We'll attach an estimated cost delta per 1M requests.

jordan: Do we need RBAC guardrails? E.g., "simulate" allowed for engineers but only ops+security can "apply" the policy.

maya: Yes. And log who ran the sim and who later applied it — full chain of custody. Export should include user id, timestamp, and workspace id.

sarah: Action items: kevin to prototype backend sim runner + staging audit sink, anne to mock modal + timeline, maya to define audit schema and export fields. I'll coordinate with product to prioritize.

kevin: I'll PR a simple sim endpoint under /internal/policy/simulate and add a feature-flag.

deploy-bot: [ci] kevin/sim-runner branch build passed (unit + integration).

sarah: Thanks everyone — let's aim to demo next Wed in the eng-platform sync. :thumbsup:
